tiers.notes: Five fast jobs on Ubuntu. With a warm cache, ~1 minute per job wall-clock.
Four jobs; the matrix job runs six cells across three OSes. The macOS cells' 10× multiplier dominates the tier's cost.
Five depth jobs on Ubuntu. The tier is gated on main, so its cost is paid once per main push, not per PR push.
Eight security jobs on Ubuntu. The tier runs on the daily schedule and on main pushes; the scheduled runs dominate the tier's cost.

optimizations.name: Concurrency cancel-in-progress
optimizations.rationale: A superseded PR push's run is cancelled; the runner is freed for the new run. The technique reduces the billed minutes for a rapid series of PR pushes.

optimizations.name: Skip CI for docs-only changes
optimizations.rationale: A change under docs/ or to a Markdown file does not trigger the CI tier. The technique eliminates the CI cost of documentation changes.

optimizations.name: Cache aggressively
optimizations.rationale: The Go module cache, the Go build cache, and the linter binary cache reduce the wall-clock of every job. The technique reduces the billed minutes proportionally.

optimizations.name: Fail-fast off, cancel-on-fail for matrix
optimizations.rationale: A matrix job with fail-fast: false reports all cells' failures in one run. The technique avoids a second run that would only re-detect the same failure.

optimizations.name: Run expensive jobs on main only
optimizations.rationale: Tier 3's depth checks are gated on main pushes. The technique pays the depth checks' cost once per main push, not once per PR push.

optimizations.name: Use Linux runners where possible
optimizations.rationale: Linux's 1× multiplier is the cheapest. The technique confines the Windows (2×) and macOS (10×) multipliers to the workflows that need them.
